newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends first 1997 trading session mixed.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends first 1997 trading session mixed.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL

PALM OIL FUTURES - Prices closed the first trading day of 1997 lower on selling and lack of support after firming in early trade on technical buying and covering. Lack of fresh factors also hit the market. March futures saw buying at 1,260 but fell back to around 1,245. Next support 1,240 and resistance 1,260.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Moved in line with futures and interest seen among nearby crude palm oil.
Palm oil prices in Malaysia ended the first trading day of 1997 mixed on lack of follow-through support and liquidation after opening higher.
Traders said the market extended Tuesday's gains at the opening on technical support.

"The market saw some renewed support after March futures surged above the 1,260 ringgit and people felt that the market would firm in near term due to underlying good fundamentals," a trader said. "But thereafter the market fell particularly in the afternoon session."
Traders had estimated output in December would fall by up to 18 percent over November, and also expect a lower end-December stock level of below 900,000 tonnes.

Falls were limited because of the bullish December export data. Cargo surveyor Societe Generale de Surveillance (SGS) Malaysia Sdn Bhd said it estimated Malaysia's palm oil exports for December at 717,197 tonnes against 700,566 tonnes in November. Caleb Brett put Malaysia's December exports at 702,082 tonnes against its estimate of 673,905 for November.
March futures closed eight ringgit lower at 1,247 ringgit ($493.66) a tonne after trading between 1,245 and 1,264.
Traders said the next resistance will be 1,260 ringgit with strong support seen at 1,245.
Among physical, Jan (south) saw offers at 1,292.50 ringgit against bids at 1,287.50, after trading at 1,290 and 1,292.50.

Jan (central) was offered at 1,277.50 and bids at 1,270. Feb (south) saw offers at 1,292.50 with bids at 1,287.50, with earlier trades at 1,290 and 1,292.50. Feb (central) was offered at 1,280 and bid at 1,270.
Among refined products, Jan RBD palm oil was offered at $537.50 a tonne FOB Malaysia, Feb/Mar at $535 and Apr/May/Jun at $532.50.
Jan RBD palm olein saw offers at $572.50, Feb/Mar at $565 and Apr/May/June at $560. Jan was traded at $571.50.
Jan RBD palm stearin was offered at $410 and Feb/Mar at $415. Jan/Feb palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $295.
